title.en: An outside test, and the last weeks of testnet

dek.en: An independent measurement finds no significant effect, Optimum answers, DSRV and Twinstake join, Korea Blockchain Week hosts CODED, and a sixth role call month passes.

en: September brought the first test of mump2p that Optimum did not run. StereumLabs measured 36 mainnet full nodes for eleven and a half days and found earlier blocks on some clients, no change on another, slower blocks on one, and overall no significant effect.

Optimum did not argue with the data; a month later it said its global acceleration had been switched on for everyone during the test, which could hide the difference, and changed how it would run. A register should keep both results, and this issue does.
On 9 September StereumLabs reported an independent test on Lido’s forum: earlier blocks on Lighthouse, Prysm and Grandine, none on Teku, slower on Nimbus, and no significant effect overall.
DSRV, with more than 300,000 staked ETH, and Twinstake joined the mump2p tests. Optimum looked ahead to Glamsterdam and a new race for data under enshrined PBS.
At Korea Blockchain Week Kent Lin spoke on staking infrastructure and Optimum co-hosted CODED with Google Cloud and Four Pillars. Four role calls named 50 members.

title.en: An independent test: no significant effect

body.en: On 9 September StereumLabs posted results on Lido’s research forum from 36 mainnet full nodes measured over eleven and a half days without validators attached. Three of six clients saw blocks earlier with mump2p, Lighthouse by about 120 ms, Prysm by about 60 ms and Grandine by 30 to 50 ms; Teku showed no change and Nimbus got slower. The author concluded there was no significant effect overall. On 12 October Optimum replied that global acceleration had been active for all nodes during the test, which may have masked the difference, and said it would limit acceleration to registered operators after 26 October.

DSRV, with more than 300,000 staked ETH and a focus on uptime, joined the mump2p tests on 10 September, and the institutional staking provider Twinstake on 15 September. On 2 September Optimum shared Node Monster’s account of its own results.

On 8 September Optimum looked at Glamsterdam, Ethereum’s next upgrade, which brings enshrined proposer builder separation. It argued that ePBS creates a new data delivery race inside each slot, and that this is where latency will matter most. On 22 September it contrasted traditional finance, where traders cut latency with colocation and private fibre, with DeFi, where the path data takes is not known in advance, so it has to be fast everywhere.

sources: Optimum on X, TradFi and DeFi

body.en: The second Asia tour began in Seoul. On 27 September Optimum attended Ethereum Korea’s Genesis event, on 28 September Kent Lin spoke on its staking infrastructure panel about why operators choose mump2p, and on 29 September Optimum co-hosted CODED with Google Cloud, Four Pillars, LINE NEXT and Auros. Médard gave an interview to Maeil Business Newspaper. On 24 September chief product officer Sajida Zouarhi spoke on a panel at ETHSofia.

On 1 September Optimum posted a five minute masterclass by Médard on why latency matters economically in DeFi and how to lower it with mathematics. On 11 September nevscape explained the value of 150 ms in 78 seconds. On 14 September Optimum shared an article on making quantum secure encryption fast enough for blockchains with RLNC. It also posted an unusual job: a trader, hired not to trade but to say what is worth building.

Flash posted role calls on 7, 14, 21 and 28 September with 50 names, among them a Chronicler on 28 September. The community was growing toward the October wave of games and tools built by members, the subject of the next back issue.

claim.en: mump2p has no significant overall effect on mainnet full nodes

note.en: StereumLabs, 36 nodes over 11.5 days, 9 September 2026. Optimum says global acceleration was on for all nodes during the test.
4 role calls in September, posted on 7, 14, 21 and 28 September by Flash in #role-announcements. Every member named has a page on the register.
